title: A transparent PNG pasted or dropped onto an ink page gets a black background
detail: readImage() in inkui.js draws every picture (paste, drop, Image… from the palette) onto a canvas and keeps it as toDataURL('image/jpeg'). JPEG has no alpha, so every transparent pixel becomes black: a diagram, a screenshot with transparency or a cut-out pasted onto a lined page shows a black box behind it on the paper.
evidence: js/core/inkui.js:1400-1413 (c.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.86) with no fill first); compare js/core/imagecrop.js:110-124 which keeps PNG/WebP or fills a background before JPEG
fix: Keep image/png when the source is PNG/WebP/GIF (or when the canvas has any alpha < 255), or fill the canvas white before drawImage when JPEG is chosen.
rootCause: Unconditional JPEG encoding of user pictures

title: Pen and ink says a pen without pressure follows 'speed and tilt'; tilt is never read

evidence: js/modules/inkset.js:56 text; grep 'tilt' js/core/ink.js js/core/inkui.js returns nothing

title: Exam Room's keep-awake is lost after the iPad is switched away and back
detail: The Exam Room requests a screen wake lock once on render. The browser releases a wake lock whenever the page is hidden (app switch, Control Centre, a notification opened); nothing re-requests it on visibilitychange, so after one switch the screen dims and locks during the countdown. KOS.desk (Focus) handles this by re-syncing on visibilitychange.
evidence: js/modules/examroom.js:154 (single navigator.wakeLock.request); compare js/core/desk.js:25-36
fix: Reuse KOS.desk's wake-lock helper, or listen for visibilitychange while the room is connected and re-request.

title: Marks by question: a question added with '＋ Question' can't be given its Max or its topic
detail: On #/exams/attempt/<uid>/marks the ＋ Question button adds a row whose only controls are Got and Redo: Max prints '—' and Topic is an empty read-only span. Only questions filled from the past-paper index carry max/refs. For a school mock, class paper or any paper not in the index (the common case) there is no way to record the out-of, so 'full marks', 'untagged · n', the total check and the post-mortem can't work, and a Redo on such a question has no leaf to be scheduled on (invariant 124 says a redo item is due on its question's leaf). Reproduced: clicking ＋ Question gave a row with inputs ['Got, question Q5', 'Redo question Q5'] and text 'Q5 | / | — | Redo'. The Topic column is therefore empty for every hand-logged attempt (dead column).

title: Timed paper: the question navigator's squares are crushed to 7px slivers on iPad and iPhone (17px on Mac)
detail: Start timed on any predicted/practice paper (#/exams/<id>/paper/1 > Start timed). The navigator holds one 30px square per question (51 here) in a flex row inside a scroller, but the squares are allowed to shrink, so instead of scrolling they are squeezed: 1-9 measure 7x44 on touch (the touch min-height makes them tall slivers with the digits overflowing into each other), 10+ 14x44; on Mac 17x30. The numbers are unreadable and the targets far below 44px wide, on the primary iPad flow for timed practice.

title: Timed paper with Rest breaks off: Pause hides the clock as 'Paused' while the paper's time keeps running, and time-up never fires while paused
detail: With Exams settings > Rest breaks off (the default), Pause logs a pause and the paper's clock keeps running (used() = now - started), but the clock text changes to 'Paused' so the remaining time disappears, and tick() skips the time-up check while s.paused. A learner can sit 'paused' past the end of the paper; on Resume the tally opens at once as 'Time is up'. Either the clock should keep counting visibly ('Paused · 1:12:04 left, the clock keeps running') or time-up should fire.
evidence: eval at mac after Pause: clock 'Paused', restBreaks undefined (off), elapsed still counting (usedSec 79); js/modules/exampaperview.js:40-44 (used()), :165 (clockEl shows 'Paused'), :169 (time-up gated on !s.paused), :188 (announce says the clock keeps running)
fix: When restBreaks is off keep showing clock(left) with a 'paused' badge, and let time-up fire regardless of s.paused.

title: Timed paper: a reload does not come back paused, contrary to the module's documented contract
detail: exampaperview.js's header says the per-device timed session is kept 'so a reload comes back paused', and timed() contains a line meant to do it, but it is a no-op (`if (!s.paused && !s.resumedHere) { s.paused = s.paused || null; }`). After a reload the clock simply carries on running. Either the comment (and docs) or the code is wrong; for an exam simulation running on is defensible, but then a reload mid-paper should at least say the clock kept going.
evidence: Started timed, reloaded: state.ui.examPaperSess.paused null, Pause button reads 'Pause', clock 2:28:15 still counting (/Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/exams-files-ink/b4-timed-reload-ipadl.png); js/modules/exampaperview.js:16-17 (comment) vs :157 (no-op)
fix: Decide the rule: set s.paused = Date.now() on a fresh page load (like Focus, invariant 4c) or remove the dead line and fix the comment.

title: 'Mark it yourself' tally: rows show only a question number and anonymous '○ ✓' chips; 'Mark schemes ›' closes the dialog and throws away every tick
detail: The tally (paper viewer > Mark an untimed attempt, or End and mark) lists 1, 2, 3 … each with chips labelled ✓ / M1 / A1 and a 0 chip, but no question text and no mark-point text, so you can only mark by flipping to the mark scheme. The only route there is 'Mark schemes ›', which closes the dialog (ov.close) and navigates — the ticks live only in the dialog's closure and are lost; after a timed paper the dialog is also the only place the session's minutes are attached. On iPad the chips are 39x26 and 25x26 (touch minimum 44). The rows also leave ~500px of empty width between the chips and the score.

title: Paper library says your PDFs 'never sync … and are never uploaded' while offering 'Keep in my cloud' and showing a 'Synced' row
detail: The 'Kept on this device' card states the library's PDFs never sync and are never uploaded, yet the same card has a 'Synced' row and each paper can be copied to the private bucket with 'Keep in my cloud' (invariant 125/150). title: Files' subject filter chips read inverted: the selected chip is the dark one, the unselected chip looks highlighted
detail: On #/files the All / CS chips are k-chip buttons with aria-pressed. The pressed rule sets background var(--s3), which in Graphite is oklch(0.14) — darker than the toolbar — while an unpressed k-chip keeps its 18% text wash. So 'All' (selected) looks like an empty hole and 'CS' (not selected) looks lit. The chips are also 31-34px wide on touch (invariant 69 floor 44) and carry no subject hue dot, unlike every other subject switch.

title: Scan pages: the four corner handles are 30px dots on iPad and iPhone, the device the camera flow is for

title: Three different file-size formatters: the same 16-byte file is '1 KB' in Files, '0 KB' in Storage and '16 B' on a topic's Files tab; Storage lists '0 KB' rows
detail: files.js rounds up to at least 1 KB, storage.js rounds down to 0 KB, attachments.js prints bytes under 1 KB. notes.txt (16 bytes) therefore shows three sizes across the app. Storage's 'By kind of data' also prints Past papers 0 KB, Your ink 0 KB and Text index 0 KB (the PDFs had been indexed — its text is under 512 bytes), zero-only supporting facts (invariant 77). The 'Free up space' card is a tall card with two lines when signed out (dead space beside 'Files in your cloud').

fix: One size formatter in KOS.ui (or KOS.files) used by all three; hide zero rows or say 'none'; let the Free up space card shrink or merge with Files in your cloud while signed out.

title: Answer pad (Write) inherits a tool its bar doesn't offer: pick Ruler on a Handwritten page and every answer pad opens with the ruler across it and no tool selected
detail: The current tool is one per-device pref (state.ui.ink.tool). A strip — the answer pad's Write mode, a flashcard's Write strip — offers only Pen, Highlight and Eraser (STRIP_TOOLS) but never clamps the tool to that set. Repro on iPad: Handwritten tab > Ruler; then Exam questions > Write. The pad draws the ruler over half its 210px height, none of the three tool buttons is checked (aria-checked=false on all), and there is no Ruler button to put it away — only tapping Pen clears it. With Lasso/Shape/Text left on, the strip would lasso or snap shapes with no visible tool.

title: Side by side on iPad landscape: the docked ink bar is 474px wide and scrolls, hiding Undo, Redo, Paper and Float behind a › arrow

title: New assessment dialog: the two-column form leaves holes (Duration, Extra time, Target grade each alone on a row) and pre-fills the Title with 'Real exam'
detail: At iPad portrait the editor is a 2-column grid but Duration, Extra time and Target grade sit alone with an empty right cell, so the 1250px dialog scrolls more than it needs. The Title field is pre-filled with the tier's name as a value (not a placeholder), so saving without typing creates an assessment literally titled 'Real exam'. title: Readiness band prints 'limiting: RAG' under 'Not enough evidence' — a limiting signal named when there is no evidence at all
detail: With thin evidence KOS.exams.readiness returns band 'thin' with limit = the first silent signal (rag). bandEl shows 'limiting: <name>' for every band except Ready, so every Season card and assessment hero reads 'Not enough evidence · limiting: RAG', which tells the learner RAG is holding the exam back when nothing has been measured. The function's own comment says the limit shows 'At risk always, for On track only with one weak signal, never Ready'. Fixture: a new mock with a 4.10 scope and no reviews or papers → band {band:'thin', limit:'rag', silent:[rag,recall,practice]}.

fix: Show the limit only for at_risk, and for on_track only when one signal is weak; for Thin say which signals are silent ('needs: recall, a timed paper').

title: A brand-new account's Exams hub is built around the Calendar's 'SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me)', migrated into a real assessment
detail: Calendar's seedSamples() adds a sample Maths mock 5 days ahead on first boot; KOS.exams.migrate() then moves every one-off calendar exam into the hub. So an empty account opens Exams & Papers on '1 assessment ahead · the next is SAMPLE — Mock exam (edit me) on Wednesday', with an 89-leaf Companion (11,400px), readiness, planner allocations, a Practice paper, a checklist and exam notices — all for an invented exam, and once migrated it is no longer flagged as a sample anywhere (the calendar event is hidden as migratedTo). The sample deadline is not migrated, so the samples split across two owners.

fix: Drop the exam from the calendar samples (the hub has its own empty state and templates), or mark samples (sample:true) and have migrate() skip them; offer a one-tap 'Remove sample data'.

title: Practice's empty state points to a '+ Log entry' button that does not exist (the button is '+ Log a result') and offers no action of its own
detail: Exams & Papers › Practice with nothing logged says 'Use “+ Log entry” after your next assessment.' The page's button is '＋ Log a result' (in the header, scrolled away on iPhone); there is no 'Log entry' anywhere, and the empty state has no button of its own. Same text for the Practice papers tab ('…after your next practice paper').

title: Start-by is too strict: a one-topic test 3 days away needing 30 minutes is born 'Start-by passed · 7 days ago' and lands in Needs attention
detail: KOS.exams.startBy rounds the run-up up to whole weeks (weeks = ceil(hoursNeeded / share)) and then adds the tier's buffer, so any non-zero need costs at least 7 days + buffer. Fixture (empty account, scope = the single leaf compsci:4.10.1): topic test in 3 days → start-by 30 Oct (passed; 0.5 h needed at 2.3 h/week); retrieval quiz in 2 days → 31 Oct (passed; 0.2 h); mock in 10 days → 2 Nov (passed; 0.6 h). Only a real exam 30 days out is not already late. The red '▼ Start-by passed · N days ago' chip and the Needs attention card therefore greet almost every short-notice assessment the moment it is created (the Calendar's sample mock shows '58 days ago' on a brand-new account), which trains the learner to ignore the alarm; the plan says start-by is advisory.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/exams-files-ink/b4-timetable-dawn-ipad.png; eval fixture {topic_test:{days:3,startBy:'2026-10-30',passed:true,why:'3 days of buffer + 0.5 h at about 2.3 h a week'}, retrieval_test:{days:2,passed:true}, mock:{days:10,passed:true}}; js/core/exams.js:543-544 (Math.ceil to weeks, then + buffer), :549 (passed); js/modules/exams.js:110, :458
fix: Compute the run-up in days (hoursNeeded / (share/7)), never put start-by before the assessment's creation date, and say 'Start now · 30 min needed' instead of 'passed' when the need still fits before the date.
rootCause: week-granular ceiling plus fixed buffer, and no floor at the creation date

title: An open dialog survives Back/hash navigation: the 'Mark it yourself' tally stayed on screen over the next pages
detail: With the tally dialog open on a paper, changing the route (browser Back, the app's ‹ › arrows, a hand-edited hash) renders the new page underneath while the modal stays open and focused — observed over #/exams/results, practice/library, scope and timetable/load. The router re-renders on popstate/hashchange without closing KOS.ui.openDialog layers, so a stale dialog (here one holding unsaved ticks for another page's paper) floats over an unrelated view.
evidence: shots taken after navigating with the tally open showed it over each page (first attempt of b4-results-ipad.png); js/core/router.js:284-306 (onPop/hashchange render with no dialog handling)
fix: On a navigation render, close (or ask about) open dialogs — or treat Back while a dialog is open as closing the dialog, as native sheets do.
